input_signals.name: Liquidity-Forced Long-Debt Issuance
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, at)), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance is a negative signal when it occurs at firms with weak cash buffers and poor operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Debt issuance can be benign for healthy firms, but for cash-poor, cash-burning firms it is more likely to reflect liquidity pressure or unfavorable financing terms. The interaction distinguishes refinancing demand under distress from ordinary leverage expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( che, at ) ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Stress Payout Cut
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), at), 1))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Payout reductions predict lower returns when firms also show poor working capital and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids betting against the payout premium directly; the signal focuses on cuts or contractions in payouts rather than payout levels. When payout retrenchment occurs under liquidity stress, it more likely reveals binding financing pressure and deteriorating prospects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( dvc, prstkc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Payout Drain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), at))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at)), NEG(RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt issuance combined with payouts predicts lower returns when firms have weak cash flow and low cash balances.
input_signals.reasoning: Borrowing while distributing cash is concerning when the firm lacks internal liquidity, because financing proceeds may be masking capital strain rather than funding productive recovery. The interaction isolates payout behavior that is unlikely to be resilient because it is paired with external debt financing and distress conditions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), rank( ratio( add( dvc, prstkc ), at ) ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ), neg( ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Funded Overexpansion Distress
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when firms are rapidly expanding assets while also facing high current-liability pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: This revision aligns with the asset-growth anomaly instead of fighting it: high asset growth is itself a low-return warning, especially if funded by debt. When expansion coincides with short-term liability pressure, new debt is more likely to amplify fragility than finance disciplined growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), sumrank( growth( at, 1 ), ratio( lct, act ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt Repurchase Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases predict lower returns when current debt is rising and operating cash flow is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Repurchases are usually interpreted as positive payout signals, but that interpretation weakens when they occur alongside short-term borrowing pressure. If cash flow is poor and current debt is increasing, buybacks may be financially strained distributions rather than credible undervaluation signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ), sumrank( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Solvency Dividend Retrenchment
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(MA(RATIO(dvc, at), 3), 1))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Smoothed dividend reductions predict lower returns when firms are highly indebted and have weak retained earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: Using a moving average of dividends reduces the influence of one-period payout noise and focuses on persistent retrenchment. A dividend reduction is more informative when solvency is already impaired, because it may reveal binding debt-overhang pressure rather than routine payout adjustment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( delta( ma( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Borrowing After Payout Retrenchment
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), SUMRANK(NEG(DELTA(MA(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), at), 3), 1)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), NEG(RATIO(re, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when firms are cutting payouts while already showing weak working capital and accumulated deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from a payout-minus-cash-flow coverage gap and instead tests whether payout retrenchment fails to solve a distressed firm’s funding need. If a firm cuts distributions but still must borrow, the debt issuance more likely reflects persistent liquidity pressure than productive financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), sumrank( neg( delta( ma( ratio( add( dvc, prstkc ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Preferred Payout Burden Under Deficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dvt, dvc), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, at)), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Preferred or non-common dividend burden predicts lower returns when firms have low cash and accumulated deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the repeated smoothed common-dividend-cut construction with a different payout mechanism: senior-like payout obligations that can drain liquidity even when common dividends are not the main issue. For cash-poor deficit firms, a high gap between total and common dividends is more likely a financing constraint burden than a healthy payout signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( dvt, dvc ), at ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( che, at ) ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Equity Conversion Dilution
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ceq, at)), NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Share-count growth predicts lower returns when distressed firms are reducing debt, consistent with dilutive debt-for-equity conversions or creditor restructurings.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the fragile sstk/(sstk+dltis) denominator and shifts away from the equity-versus-debt issuance-mix signal. The interaction is specifically between dilution and debt reduction under weak solvency, where existing shareholders may suffer value transfer to creditors despite lower reported leverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( ceq, at ) ), neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity Raise During Dividend Suspension
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(dvc, at), 3)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at)), NEG(RATIO(che, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance predicts lower returns when firms have effectively suspended dividends and have weak retained earnings and cash reserves.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the dividend-restoration idea, which had conflicting cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, with a distress-financing mechanism tied to dividend absence rather than dividend increases. Equity raised by cash-poor deficit firms that cannot sustain common dividends is more likely dilutive survival capital than a credible recovery signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), sumrank( neg( ma( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ), neg( ratio( che, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Preferred Payout Debt Overhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dvt, dvc), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Preferred or non-common dividend burden predicts lower returns when firms are highly indebted and have weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This preserves the preferred-payout burden mechanism but changes the economic conditioner from the earlier low-cash/deficit screen to debt-overhang and current cash-generation weakness. Senior-like distributions are especially damaging when operating cash flow is insufficient and debt claims are already large.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( dvt, dvc ), at ) ), sumrank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt Proceeds Liquidity Leak
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(dltis, at), DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1))), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt issuance predicts lower returns when borrowing is not retained as cash and the firm faces current-liability pressure with weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg measures debt proceeds net of the contemporaneous change in cash, aiming to identify borrowing that is immediately consumed rather than strengthening liquidity. This is most concerning when current liabilities are high and operating cash flow is weak, suggesting debt is filling a short-term funding hole.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ratio( dltis, at ), delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt Funded Dividend Hike
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(dvc, at), 3), 1)), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Dividend increases predict lower returns when they coincide with rising current debt and falling cash balances.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids simply mirroring the earlier dividend-restoration signal’s cash-flow conditioner and instead asks whether the payout increase appears short-term financed. A dividend hike is a poor recovery signal if it occurs while current debt rises and cash is depleted, suggesting costly signaling or liquidity strain rather than sustainable restoration.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ma( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ), 1 ) ), sumrank( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Funded Senior Payout Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, dvc), at), 1))), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt issuance predicts lower returns when firms also carry preferred or non-common dividend burdens under liquidity pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: This separates senior-like payout obligations from ordinary common payouts. New borrowing used in a firm with weak operating cash flow, high current-liability pressure, and preferred payout burden is more likely supporting prior claims than improving common-equity recovery.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, dvc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Senior-Common Payout Squeeze
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, dvc), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(MA(RATIO(dvc, at), 3), 1)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Preferred or non-common payout burden predicts lower returns when common dividends are being cut and firms have debt overhang with weak cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: The mechanism is a redistribution of payout capacity away from common shareholders toward senior-like claims. When common dividends retrench while preferred obligations persist, highly indebted cash-flow-weak firms may be signaling deeper common-equity impairment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, dvc ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( delta( ma( ratio( dvc, at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Credit-Rationed Rollover Shortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(dltis, lct))), SUMRANK(RATIO(lct, act), NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Low long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when firms face high current-liability pressure and weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the debt-proceeds-leak construction and tests the opposite failure mode: distressed firms may be unable to secure term financing at all. When current obligations are large and cash generation is weak, unusually low long-term borrowing relative to current liabilities can signal credit rationing or an impending rollover problem.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( dltis, lct ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( lct, act ), neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent External-Finance Cash Burn
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(dltis, sstk), at), 3)), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), NEG(MA(RATIO(wcap, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent reliance on debt and equity issuance predicts lower returns when operating cash flow and working capital remain persistently weak.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the contemporaneous dual-issuance recombination with a persistence mechanism, reducing dependence on one-period lumpy issuance flows. Repeated external financing under sustained cash-flow and working-capital weakness is more likely a continuing funding deficit than opportunistic capital raising.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_sum( ratio( add( dltis, sstk ), at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), neg( ma( ratio( wcap, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Senior-Claim Debt-Service Drain
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltr, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, dvc), at), 1))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at)), RATIO(lct, act)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt repayment predicts lower returns when firms also carry senior-like payout burdens and face weak cash flow with current-liability pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the equity-issuance-plus-debt-repayment family and focuses on cash being absorbed by senior claims. For firms with weak operating cash flow and high short-term obligations, servicing debt while maintaining preferred or non-common payouts can leave common equity with deteriorating residual value.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( rank( ratio( dltr, at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, dvc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ), ratio( lct, act ) ) )
